title: Qualcomm's AI Infrastructure Pivot Is Underappreciated
author: Marc Guberti
description: Qualcomm is positioning itself for significant growth in 2027 through its pivot into AI infrastructure, with deals secured from Amazon and Meta Platforms. The company expects non-handset revenue to grow over 60% in fiscal 2027 and projects a $200 billion CPU market opportunity by fiscal 2029, yet trades at a modest 23 P/E ratio that undervalues its growth potential.

Stock valuation appears underappreciated relative to growth prospects.

title: Department of Energy Announces a New Multi-Billion-Dollar Nuclear Energy Deal
author: Neha Chamaria
description: The Department of Energy announced a $4.2 billion loan commitment to Vistra to extend and upgrade three nuclear plants in Pennsylvania and Ohio, preserving 4 GW of power and adding 433 MW of new capacity. This deal is part of Trump's broader initiative to quadruple U.S. nuclear capacity to 400 GW by 2050. Meta has already signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with Vistra for 2,609 MW from these plants, highlighting how existing reactor owners are positioned to benefit most from the nuclear renaissance driven by AI energy demands.

title: Why I Don't Think Meta's AI Strategy Will Be Successful
author: David Jagielski, Cpa
description: Meta's recent launch of its personal AI agent Muse has boosted the stock 12% this year, but analyst David Jagielski argues the gains won't last. He cites Meta's poor privacy track record as a major obstacle to user trust in AI agents that require access to sensitive information. Additionally, the stock trades at a premium P/E of 28 versus the S&P 500 average of 23, making it vulnerable to decline given risks from its AI strategy and money-losing metaverse segment.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Author expresses skepticism about Meta's AI strategy success due to the company's poor privacy track record, which undermines user trust needed for AI agents. Additionally, the stock is overvalued at a P/E of 28 relative to market average, and faces risks from costly metaverse investments, making it vulnerable to significant decline.

title: History Says Infrastructure Booms Create Winners and Losers. Here Are 3 AI Cloud Stocks to Watch.

title: Here's Why SpaceX's AI Infrastructure in Space "Moonshot" Won't Uproot Neocloud Companies
author: Marc Guberti
description: SpaceX launched a test satellite with Google's TPUs to explore orbital data centers, but satellite-based data centers will cost 2.5-3x more than Earth-based facilities. Tech giants need computing power immediately and are investing heavily in neocloud companies like Nebius and Iren, which have available megawatt capacity and scaling pipelines. Orbital data centers are unlikely to replace terrestrial data centers in the near term.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While SpaceX achieved a milestone launching Google's TPUs, the article emphasizes significant cost barriers (2.5-3x more expensive) and Elon Musk's history of missing ambitious timelines. The technology is promising but faces substantial hurdles before commercial viability.

Alphabet is actively testing orbital data center technology through Project Suncatcher, showing innovation leadership. However, the article suggests this is a long-term bet while immediate compute needs are being met through terrestrial solutions.
